submissions.title: Amazon responds to data center backlash, says it no longer uses NDAs
submissions.excerpt: Amazon pledged more than $1 billion over five years for US communities that host its data centers
submissions.note: Not tied to a single project — flagging as background relevant to the siting-restriction side of the tracker. Amazon said AWS has stopped requiring local officials to sign NDAs before green-lighting data center projects, and launched a 'Built Together' program pledging $1B+ over five years to host communities (community-college funding, energy-efficiency upgrades for schools/homes), plus a 'Data Center Commitment' not to raise local electricity bills and to publish annual energy/water-use figures. This is a genuine reversal: a Sept 28, 2026 PolitiFact piece on an Ohio legislative hearing had Amazon, Google and Meta declining to make the NDA-ending promise Microsoft made in March 2026. Multiple independent outlets (Semafor Oct 2, TechCrunch/Manila Times/Hoodline Oct 3) corroborate the date. CAUTION: outbound fetch was blocked for every external domain this run (confirmed against tracker.bepresearch.com, example.com, sec.gov, businesswire, prnewswire, github.com's main site, etc. — only the search tool and api.github.com worked), so this excerpt is paraphrased from secondary coverage, not pulled verbatim from the primary announcement; confirm exact wording before citing.

submissions.title: Lansing City Council approves 182-day moratorium on new data centers
submissions.excerpt: a 182-day moratorium... begins on July 27 and will go until January 25, 2027
submissions.note: SITING RESTRICTION: Lansing, Michigan city council passed a 182-day moratorium (7-1 vote) pausing new data center building permits and zoning applications, effective July 27, 2026 through January 25, 2027 — prompted after the 'Deep Green' data center proposal for downtown Lansing fell through in April 2026. Deep Green does not appear in the current 103-project tracker snapshot, so this is a general-purpose restriction not yet linked to any tracked project. submissions.title: Data centers draw backlash, lawsuit in Guadalupe County as residents raise transparency concerns
submissions.excerpt: Palomino Alpha requesting a contract providing the data center 500,000 gallons of water a day
submissions.note: SITING RESTRICTION / legal challenge, and two possibly-new projects. The Data Center Action Coalition and Guadalupe County, TX residents sued county commissioners (~July 20, 2026) alleging Texas Open Meetings Act and conflict-of-interest violations in approving tax abatements and development agreements for two data centers: 'CloudBurst Texas' (~$500M tax abatement, 700+ acres, approved April 2026) and 'Palomino Alpha' (reportedly seeking 500,000 gal/day from Crystal Clear Special Utility District; suit alleges the county judge's family owns 186 acres being sold to the project). Neither CloudBurst Texas nor Palomino Alpha appears in the current 103-project tracker snapshot — suggesting both as candidate new projects, with this lawsuit as the first siting-risk source on each. Same caveats as the other findings here: not within the usual 24-72h window, paraphrased excerpt (outbound fetch blocked this run, not pulled verbatim), and no local way to check for an existing restrictions record.
